lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked twelve-string guitar, a soft cymbal]

[Verse 1: lead voice, the group echoes each line]
Ice on the inside (ice on the inside)
Of the window pane (of the window pane)
I put on two sweaters (I put on two sweaters)
And I walk in the rain (walk in the rain)

[Chorus: four-part harmony, full band]
Somewhere it's warm (somewhere it's warm)
Somebody's sleeves are rolled
Somewhere it's warm
And I'm here in the cold
Dreaming of somewhere, somewhere it's warm

[Verse 2: lead voice, the group echoes]
There's a laundromat on Fourth Street (laundromat on Fourth Street)
With the dryers going round (the dryers going round)
I sit there with a paperback (sit there with a paperback)
The lady lets me stay (she lets me stay)

[Chorus: four-part harmony, full band]
Somewhere it's warm (somewhere it's warm)
Somebody's sleeves are rolled
Somewhere it's warm
And I'm here in the cold
Dreaming of somewhere, somewhere it's warm

[Flute Solo: breathy alto flute, over the verse chords]

[Verse 3: lead voice, the group echoes, more urgent]
If I had the bus fare (if I had the bus fare)
I'd be gone today (I'd be gone today)
But somebody needs me (somebody needs me)
So I guess I'll stay (I guess I'll stay)

[Final Chorus: four-part harmony, held last chord]
Somewhere it's warm (somewhere it's warm)
Somebody's sleeves are rolled
Somewhere it's warm
And I'm here in the cold
Dreaming of somewhere
Somewhere it's warm
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 112 BPM, 4/4, C-sharp minor. A brisk folk-rock pulse under a cool, wistful minor-key tune.

VOICE: Two men and two women. A male tenor sings each line of the verse and the other three echo it a moment later in harmony, with a strong, clear female alto prominent. The choruses are full four-part harmony, bright on top and warm underneath, ending on a long held chord.

INSTRUMENTS: A fingerpicked acoustic twelve-string guitar. A breathy alto flute for the solo. A steady, simple drum kit. Electric bass. A second, strummed acoustic guitar. A little electric guitar with tremolo. Tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, twelve-string guitar. 0:10 Verse 1 with echoes. 0:34 Chorus 1. 0:56 Verse 2. 1:20 Chorus 2. 1:42 Flute solo. 1:58 Verse 3. 2:16 Final chorus, ending on a held chord at 2:38.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1960s Los Angeles folk-rock: bright guitars, voices stacked and slightly reverberant, a clean, simple rhythm section.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first echoed line at 0:12.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Verse 3 is the adult reason for staying: somebody needs me. The original's narrator is free to go and only lacks the nerve. This one has obligations, and dreams anyway.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Cold, longing, duty, longing still.
